objective: Start class with a predictable entry sequence

detailedDescription: Use this toolkit to teach and review one classroom routine. It provides concrete language, original decision cases, and tools for recording observations without public ranking. This is not a grade-specific academic worksheet, a state-standard alignment claim, an individualized intervention, or a crisis plan.

2 classroom activity plans plus 1 learner-response page and 1 reflection page
1 teacher response plan, 1 private observation form, and 1 neutral-observation response guide

minutes: 20–30 minutes of adult preparation; two 15–20-minute rehearsal activities; brief reviews across one week.

title: Rhyme Circle: Listen, Match, Invent
subject: Phonological awareness
standard: Pre-K RF 2(a)
objective: With adult support, recognize and generate spoken rhymes.
publicationStatus: Available for purchase. Full PDF unlocks after verified payment.
thumbnailAlt: KSP-branded cover of Rhyme Circle: Listen, Match, Invent.
summary: With adult support, recognize and generate spoken rhymes. Includes models, practice, exit check, and answer guidance.
detailedDescription: Rhyme Circle: Listen, Match, Invent gives Pre-K learners a focused route from explicit modeling to supported practice and independent application. A rhyme has the same ending sound, even when its spelling differs. Say each pair naturally, then stretch the ending. Children may answer by speaking, pointing to a yes/no card, or giving a thumbs signal. Adults read every word; printed-word reading is not expected. Accept a playful invented word if its ending genuinely rhymes, then model a real word. Use four prompts per sitting.

detailedDescription: Pronoun Repair Shop: Case and Clarity gives Grade 6 learners a focused route from explicit modeling to supported practice and independent application. Use subject forms for the doer (I, she, he, we, they); object forms after a verb or preposition (me, her, him, us, them); possessive forms to show belonging (my/mine, her/hers, our/ours). For a compound, temporarily remove the other noun to hear the case. Name an unclear referent instead of guessing. This is focused practice within L.SS.6.1.

title: Textual Evidence Detectives: Citing Evidence in Literary Text
subject: Reading
standard: RL.7.1 — Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
objective: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of explicit statements and inferences drawn from literary text.
publicationStatus: Available for purchase. Full PDF unlocks after verified payment.
description: Read an original story about a community garden under threat; cite explicit and inferred evidence across warm-up, guided practice, independent practice, small-group work, and an exit ticket.
summary: A complete RL.7.1 practice packet with original fiction passage, evidence organizer, multiple-choice, open-response, intervention support, enrichment challenge, exit ticket, and full answer key.
detailedDescription: Students read an original 7-paragraph fiction passage about a teacher who fights to save a community garden. The packet moves from a 5-minute warm-up through a teacher-guided evidence organizer, independent multiple-choice and open-response questions, differentiated small-group tasks (intervention sentence frame + enrichment analytical paragraph), and a self-assessed exit ticket. The answer key includes worked explanations for every multiple-choice item and detailed scoring guidance for every open-response question, plus AIG, 504, EC, and ESL differentiation notes.
included: 1 original fiction passage (7 paragraphs, approx. 950L)
Warm-up (2 questions)
Guided practice with evidence organizer graphic (3 tasks)
Independent practice (5 questions: 3 MC + 2 open-response)
Small-group work (intervention sentence frame + enrichment challenge)
Exit ticket with self-assessment scale
Complete answer key with scoring guidance and differentiation notes
minutes: 45–60 minutes (or split across two class periods)
studentDirections: Read the passage carefully, noting the paragraph numbers. Use evidence from the text to support every answer. Quote or closely paraphrase the text and include the paragraph number.
teacherUse: Use the warm-up as a bell-ringer. Work through the evidence organizer together before releasing students to independent practice. Use the exit ticket to determine next-day groupings.
answerKey: Worked explanations for all multiple-choice items; detailed scoring guidance for all open-response questions; differentiation notes for AIG, 504, EC, and ESL learners.
preparation: Print pages 1-7 for students. Keep page 8 (answer key) for teacher use only. Review the evidence organizer before class.
digitalNotes: Print US Letter at actual size. Separate student pages from the answer key before distributing.

accessibility.EC: Pre-teach: explicit, inference, textual evidence. Provide sentence frame for all open-response. Allow oral responses.
accessibility.ESL: Preview key vocabulary: demolished, petition, council, preserve. Allow bilingual glossary. Pair for Q5 before independent writing.

title: Theme Trackers: Determining Theme and Writing an Objective Summary
subject: Reading
standard: RL.7.2 — Determine a theme of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.
objective: Determine the theme of a literary text, analyze how it develops across the text using textual evidence, and write an objective summary.
publicationStatus: Available for purchase. Full PDF unlocks after verified payment.
description: Read an original story about a student who discovers the value of persistence; trace theme development across 12 paragraphs through vocabulary preview, guided organizer, partner discussion, independent practice, small-group work, and exit ticket.

detailedDescription: Students read an original 12-paragraph fiction passage about a reluctant robotics team member who learns the value of persistence. The 80-minute packet includes a vocabulary preview table, prior knowledge warm-up, annotated reading with quick check, teacher-guided Theme Tracker organizer, structured partner discussion with sentence starters, 8 independent questions (4 MC + 4 open-response including a full objective summary task), differentiated small-group work (2 intervention frames + 2 enrichment challenges), and a 3-part exit ticket with objective summary checklist and 4-level self-assessment. The answer key includes worked explanations for every MC item, detailed scoring guidance for every open-response question, and AIG/504/EC/ESL differentiation notes.
